profile.headline: Software Engineer at Pinterest
profile.summary:
SWE at Pinterest, ex-Amazon.
BS in both Mathematics and Computer Science and a BA in Statistics from the University of Chicago.

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
•	Helped Dr. Junchen Jiang and his research team develop a custom video streaming protocol that improves both bandwidth consumption and object detection accuracy.
•	Developed strategies and code for cropping and merging images to minimize the number of frames sent to the neural network for object detection while maintaining accuracy.
•	Created online surveys with Node.js and ran them on MTurk users to determine which video playback issue, such as buffering or lowering resolution, may least negatively affect user experience.

company.name: University of Chicago Department of Computer Science

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description:
•	Worked on the Third-Party Integrations team in an Agile environment with two-week sprints and daily standups and code reviews, completing tickets alongside the other software developers on the team.
•	Developed APIs and corresponding unit tests for their Python codebase to determine which teachers have students with no password in the SQL server database.

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description:
•	Worked on the Cloud API team to split their highest-traffic service into two separate microservices, allowing for greater horizontal scalability.
•	Refactored API and updated SQL calls to keep in line with MVC paradigm to make codebase easier to read and maintain, creating new unit tests using JUnit and RxJava during this process.
•	Implemented a linter for their Java codebase that failed builds upon any unconformity with our presets, forcing consistent, objective coding style across the team.

positions.title: Research Intern
positions.description:
•	Worked with a mechanical engineering professor and his PhD student to develop an easy method to create model spines for scoliotic patients.
•	Wrote an abstract for the results of the simulation on the scoliotic spines vs. healthy spines.
•	Submitted thesis and presented at a conference held by the Orthopaedic Research Society in Houston
